title: Causal Link Evidence Matrix
description: Machine-readable evidence matrix documenting all causal links tested in DSCNS Phase 6 (Causal Link Verification)

causal_links.name: Experience → Policy
causal_links.description: Accumulated experience in memory causes policy distribution to diverge from experience-free baseline
causal_links.hypothesis: The presence of experience memory causes measurable divergence in the policy distribution compared to a system without memory
causal_links.interpretation: Memory provides subtle but statistically significant policy modulation. The small KL value suggests cautious experience integration.
causal_links.significance: Foundational — without this link, no learning from history is possible

causal_links.name: Policy → Target
causal_links.description: Policy directs modification toward specific targets at a rate above random chance
causal_links.hypothesis: The policy selects modification targets with accuracy significantly above chance level
causal_links.interpretation: Policy achieves 31.8% above-chance target selection, demonstrating meaningful spatial guidance for modifications.
causal_links.significance: Essential — determines WHERE modifications are applied

causal_links.name: Policy → Magnitude
causal_links.hypothesis: There exists a monotonic relationship between policy magnitude parameter and actual modification magnitude
causal_links.interpretation: Perfect monotonic relationship confirms the policy magnitude parameter is deterministically controlling modification intensity. No stochasticity in the magnitude pathway.
causal_links.significance: Enables nuanced control — system can make fine-grained adjustments

causal_links.name: Modification → Outcome
causal_links.description: Policy-guided modifications produce better outcomes than unguided modifications
causal_links.hypothesis: Modifications guided by the policy produce lower (better) Relative Feature Rate than modifications without policy guidance
causal_links.interpretation: Policy-guided modifications achieve 7.9% better outcomes. Improvement is real but modest, suggesting policy guidance provides limited advantage.
causal_links.significance: Validates the output quality of the entire upstream chain

causal_links.name: Outcome → Credit
causal_links.description: Outcomes generate non-zero credit signals quantifying their contribution
causal_links.hypothesis: Outcomes produce credit signals that quantify their contribution to system performance
causal_links.interpretation: NoCredit correctly disables credits (mean=0), but FullPolicy credits are extremely weak and inconsistent. The credit computation exists but is not robust.
causal_links.significance: Critical feedback link — weak credits prevent learning from outcomes
known_issues: Reward signal may be too sparse

causal_links.name: Credit → Policy
causal_links.description: Credit signals cause measurable policy changes
causal_links.hypothesis: Credit signals influence policy updates, causing alignment between credit and policy change
causal_links.interpretation: Zero alignment between credit signals and policy changes. The policy does not respond to credit at all. This is the most critical failure in the feedback loop.
causal_links.significance: Without this link, no feedback-driven learning occurs
root_causes: Missing/disconnected gradient pathways between credit and policy
Policy update mechanism may not receive credit as input
recommendations: Verify gradient flow from credit to policy parameters
Debug EAR computation for measurement artifacts

causal_links.name: Full Closed Loop
causal_links.description: Complete experience→policy→modification→outcome→credit→policy cycle functions as self-reinforcing feedback
causal_links.hypothesis: The complete feedback loop functions end-to-end, enabling autonomous self-correction
causal_links.interpretation: The full closed loop cannot function because the feedback pathway (Outcome→Credit→Policy) is broken. The system operates as a one-shot pipeline, not a self-correcting mechanism.
causal_links.significance: The ultimate goal of DSCNS — autonomous self-correction — is not achieved

link_supported.description: Quantitative evidence exceeds threshold; causal link experimentally verified

policy_divergence.description: KL divergence between FullPolicy and each ablation condition

FullPolicy_vs_FrozenPolicy.interpretation: Largest divergence — frozen weights significantly alter policy behavior

FullPolicy_vs_NoMemory.interpretation: Small but non-zero — memory provides subtle policy modulation

FullPolicy_vs_NoCredit.interpretation: Negligible — credit removal has no policy effect; policy is insensitive to credit

FullPolicy_vs_NoOutcomeReward.interpretation: Negligible — outcome reward removal has no policy effect

conditions.name: FullPolicy
conditions.description: Complete system with all components enabled

conditions.name: FrozenPolicy
conditions.description: Frozen model weights, no learning during training

conditions.name: NoModification
conditions.description: No modifications applied to the system

conditions.name: MemoryOnly
conditions.description: Memory present but no policy update from memory

conditions.name: CreditOnly
conditions.description: Credit computed but no policy update from credit

self_correction.description: Full closed loop (L7) cannot be verified due to broken feedback pathway
self_correction.recommendation: Fix credit assignment (L5) and credit→policy pathway (L6) before re-evaluating
